name: HelpGuide
texts: Everything this blog can do, and where each thing lives. Start at the top if it is a new site; jump to a section if you are looking something up.First five minutes1Name the siteTitle, logo, language and menu in Settings → Site. It is live the moment you save.2Write the first postMarkdown and a toolbar. Save keeps it a draft; Publish puts it on the site.3Choose the lookSix palettes, a font, and text sizes per role. Readers can switch palette themselves.4Turn on what you needSMTP for the newsletter, Google Drive for backups, Cloudflare for the edge cache.5Gather readersOnce SMTP is set, a sign-up form appears on the site. Sending is always your call.WritingMediaReadersAnalyticsSettingsServerCacheMCPMarkdownTroubleshootingWriting & publishingMarkdown plus a toolbar. Drafts autosave in your browser and only reach the site when you Save or Publish, so editing a live post never pushes half-finished text.Schedule by publishing with a future date: the post stays hidden and goes live on time. It does not email anyone by itself.The last 3 versions of every post are kept; restore one from the editor.Series group related posts in order, with prev/next links and a /series/… page.Every delete is a soft delete. Nothing is ever removed automatically — Trash is emptied by hand.New postAll contentTrashMedia & filesDrop an image into the editor or the Library. Responsive AVIF and WebP versions plus a thumbnail are generated for you; the original is always kept.The Library flags unused files (nothing links them) so a clear-out is safe. It only reports — it never deletes.Files live on your server's own disk, served from /uploads. No object-storage account.Open LibraryReaders — comments & newsletterBoth are off until you set them up, and both are yours: no third-party service sits between you and your readers.Comments — enable in Settings → Content. Optional Turnstile anti-spam and Google sign-in. Replying emails the person you replied to.Newsletter — add your SMTP details in Settings → Integrations and a sign-up form appears at the foot of every post plus a button in the site header. Sign-up is double opt-in: the address only counts once it clicks the confirmation link.Sending is always manual. Nothing is emailed automatically, not even a scheduled post going live. You tick the posts, read the real email in the preview, and press send. Tick several and they go out as one digest, not one message each.Newsletter → People shows what each address actually received, any SMTP failure with its error, and the open rate. Newsletter → Test sends you a sample of each email before a reader ever sees one.NewsletterCommentsSMTP settingsAnalyticsNo cookies, no personal data. A visitor is a salted hash of IP + user agent, and the raw user agent is never stored — only coarse device / browser / OS buckets.Bots, admin pages and your own visits are skipped, so the numbers are readers.Views, scroll depth and dwell time; traffic sources; per-post drill-down. Kept forever — no rolling window.Open AnalyticsSettingsOne form, one Save, applied site-wide with no redeploy. Five tabs:Site — title, logo, header menu, language, content width.Content — reader features (search, contents, sidebar, related, book mode…) and comments.Appearance — palettes, fonts, per-role text sizes, custom CSS.SEO — sitemap, RSS, robots, OG images, URL redirects.Integrations — SMTP, MCP, Google Drive backups, Cloudflare, WordPress import, comment keys.Open SettingsServer, backups & upgradesRuns entirely on your own server: two SQLite files for content and analytics, the local filesystem for images. Native or Docker, no cloud account./api/health reports the database and the storage directory separately — point your uptime monitor at it. Boot fails fast on a missing required setting.Backups: scheduled snapshots (both databases + every file) written to your own disk, plus a download-now archive. Settings → System → Backups.Upgrades apply tracked SQL migrations, so a schema change runs once and only once.Self-host guideBackupsCloudflare & cachePut Cloudflare in front for TLS and a global edge cache — the big win when readers are far from your server.Cache Rules: bypass /admin and /api, cache everything else at the origin TTL. Turn Rocket Loader off (it breaks React). SSL: Full (Strict).Add a Cloudflare API token + Zone ID in Settings → Integrations and every save purges the zone automatically.Clear all cache (sidebar) purges the origin and Cloudflare, then re-warms the home and newest pages.After deploying code, flush the edge with GET /api/cron?purge=1. Cloudflare caches HTML, so a stale page is not something a reader can refresh away.Cache RulesSEO & cachingMCP — let an AI run the blogThe built-in MCP server gives an AI agent the same rules as the admin: create and update posts and pages, manage media and settings, everything revalidated and written to the activity log exactly like a human action. Turn it on and mint access tokens in Settings → Integrations — tokens are shown once and stored hashed.MCP docsIntegrationsActivity logMarkdown the editor understandsStandard Markdown, plus these. name: ReadersSection
texts: Readers — comments & newsletterBoth are off until you set them up, and both are yours: no third-party service sits between you and your readers.Comments — enable in Settings → Content. Optional Turnstile anti-spam and Google sign-in. Replying emails the person you replied to.Newsletter — add your SMTP details in Settings → Integrations and a sign-up form appears at the foot of every post plus a button in the site header. Sign-up is double opt-in: the address only counts once it clicks the confirmation link.Sending is always manual. Nothing is emailed automatically, not even a scheduled post going live. You tick the posts, read the real email in the preview, and press send. Tick several and they go out as one digest, not one message each.Newsletter → People shows what each address actually received, any SMTP failure with its error, and the open rate. Newsletter → Test sends you a sample of each email before a reader ever sees one.NewsletterCommentsSMTP settings

name: ServerSection
texts: Server, backups & upgradesRuns entirely on your own server: two SQLite files for content and analytics, the local filesystem for images. Native or Docker, no cloud account./api/health reports the database and the storage directory separately — point your uptime monitor at it. Boot fails fast on a missing required setting.Backups: scheduled snapshots (both databases + every file) written to your own disk, plus a download-now archive. Settings → System → Backups.Upgrades apply tracked SQL migrations, so a schema change runs once and only once.Self-host guideBackups

name: TroubleTable
texts: SymptomWhat to doAn edit is live on the origin but readers still see the old pageCloudflare caches HTML. Use Clear all cache in the sidebar — a browser refresh cannot fix an edge cache.Test SMTP fails with "wrong version number"Port and TLS disagree. 465 is implicit TLS (tick the box); 587 and 25 are STARTTLS (leave it unticked).A subscriber signed up but got no emailThe row is saved before the mail is sent, so the sign-up survives a bad SMTP. Check Newsletter → People for the failure, then Newsletter → Test.A scheduled post did not go live on timeIts cron must be hitting /api/cron?publish=1 with the CRON_SECRET bearer.Sign-in silently returns to the homepageThat Google account is not AUTHORIZED_EMAIL. Only that one address reaches the admin.An old URL 404s after a renameRenaming adds a 301 automatically. If the URL never existed here, add one in Settings → SEO → Redirects.Images vanished after a restoreCheck /api/health — it reports the database and the storage directory separately.
